case_title.quote: STATE OF GUJARAT & ANR. v. NARAYAN @ NARAYAN SAI @ MOTA BHAGWAN
case_title.reason: Matches the title, apart from a spacing glitch in 'Mota'.

number_of_accused.quote: An FIR ... was registered against the respondent

accused_gender.quote: respondent ... the only son of his father

accused_age.reason: No age of the respondent is given in the judgment.

accused_occupation.reason: Occupation is not stated (references to sadhaks and followers do not state it).

previous_criminal_record.correct_value: Two other criminal cases pending (bail granted); seven offences registered; allegations of witness intimidation and bribery are disputed and not proven
previous_criminal_record.quote: apart from the present case, he is accused in two other offences in which he has been granted bail
previous_criminal_record.reason: Mixes in jail misconduct and unproven allegations; no prior convictions are stated.

accused_victim_relationship.reason: The relationship is not described in this judgment.

offence_category.reason: Rape offences are the main conviction.

statutory_provisions.reason: Omits s.323 on which conviction was also recorded.

weapon.reason: No weapon used by the accused in the offence is mentioned.

evidence_type.reason: The judgment does not discuss the evidence type at trial.

confession.reason: No mention of a confession either way.

aggravating_circumstances.correct_value: Allegations in the DGP's order: witness threats and attacks by followers, bribery attempts, mass following, mobile phone in jail
aggravating_circumstances.quote: mass following of the respondent willing to commit offences at the instance of the respondent
aggravating_circumstances.reason: Broadly right, but these are allegations considered for furlough, not established aggravating factors.

mitigating_circumstances.correct_value: Released in Dec 2020 for mother's health; surrendered on time; High Court found no incident during furlough (disputed by State)
mitigating_circumstances.quote: No untoward incident took place after the respondent was released in December 2020
mitigating_circumstances.reason: Roughly right; the SC did not accept the 'no illegal activity' point as decisive.

trial_court_outcome.correct_value: Convicted on 30 April 2019; life imprisonment under ss.376(2) and 377, plus other sentences, fines, Rs 5,00,000 compensation, concurrent
trial_court_outcome.quote: the Sessions Court by a judgment dated 30 April 2019 convicted the respondent

high_court_outcome.quote: The Single Judge directed the release of the respondent on furlough.

final_outcome.correct_value: State's appeal allowed; HC order granting furlough set aside
final_outcome.quote: we allow the appeal and set aside the impugned judgment and order of the High Court
final_outcome.reason: No acquittal; the conviction stands and furlough is denied.

offence_finally_established.reason: Convictions subsist; the SC did not disturb them.

imprisonment_type.correct_value: Life imprisonment (with rigorous imprisonment for lesser offences)
imprisonment_type.reason: Imprisonment continues; the field is not 'none'.

imprisonment_years.quote: life imprisonment together with a fine of Rs. 1,00,000/-
imprisonment_years.reason: A life sentence stands, so null is wrong.

fine_rs.correct_value: Rs. 1,00,000 each under ss.376(2) and 377, plus smaller fines on other counts
fine_rs.quote: life imprisonment together with a fine of Rs. 1,00,000/-
fine_rs.reason: Fines were imposed, so null is wrong.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Respondent convicted of rape etc., sentenced to life; applied for furlough on 17 March 2021; DGP rejected it on 8 May 2021; HC allowed furlough; State appealed
neutral_facts.quote: The application was rejected by the Director General of Police ... on 8 May 2021.
neutral_facts.reason: Omits core procedural facts and presents contested allegations as fact; 'no illegal activities during furlough' is a High Court finding.

offence_severity.quote: Section 376(2): life imprisonment together with a fine of Rs. 1,00,000/-

physical_harm.correct_value: Harm to witnesses by third parties (assaults, acid attack, a witness died); respondent's involvement only alleged
physical_harm.quote: The witness suffered severe injury and died during treatment
physical_harm.reason: Harm was caused by others, and the respondent's link is unproven.

number_of_offences.correct_value: Convicted under seven provisions (ss.376(2), 377, 354, 504, 506(2), 508, 323); seven other offences are registered against his followers
number_of_offences.quote: seven offences have been registered against him
number_of_offences.reason: Seven registered offences are cited, but the convicted offences are not mentioned.

financial_property_loss.reason: No financial loss is relevant or stated.

premeditation_planning.quote: An attempt has been made to threaten and suborn the investigating team and the witnesses.
premeditation_planning.reason: The court made no premeditation finding about the offence.

motive.reason: No motive is identified for the offences.

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: SC found the DGP's reasons not perverse; threats, bribery attempts, jail conduct not above reproach support apprehension of public disorder
key_evidence_accepted.quote: The conduct after the trial, in jail, has not been shown to be above reproach.
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Overstates: SC did not accept that he murdered witnesses, only that the circumstances supported apprehension.

witness_credibility.correct_value: No credibility assessment; the SC noted attempts to threaten and suborn witnesses and jail conduct not above reproach
witness_credibility.quote: An attempt has been made to threaten and suborn the investigating team and the witnesses.
witness_credibility.reason: Not a credibility assessment of witnesses.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Temporary bail in 2015 and 2019; furlough from 5 Dec 2020; temporary bail 31 Jan–3 Feb 2021 and surrendered; jail conduct questioned
post_offence_conduct.quote: The conduct after the trial, in jail, has not been shown to be above reproach.
post_offence_conduct.reason: Dates are accurate, but the jail misconduct allegation is omitted and the 'furlough then interim bail' sequence is garbled.

custody_duration.quote: The respondent has been under imprisonment for a period of seven and a half years.

bail_history.correct_value: Temporary bail 3 weeks from 16 April 2015; 2 days from 15 Feb 2019; furlough from 5 Dec 2020; temporary bail 31 Jan–3 Feb 2021
bail_history.quote: released on temporary bail for a period of three weeks on 16 April 2015

trial_duration.correct_value: FIR 6 Oct 2013; trial judgment 30 April 2019; HC furlough judgment 24 June 2021; SC decision 20 Oct 2021
trial_duration.reason: The HC date is mislabelled and the SC date is wrong (24 June 2021 is the HC judgment).

legal_representation.quote: Tushar Mehta, SG, Kanu Agrawal, Aniruddha P. Mayee, Advs. for the Appellants.

investigation_status.correct_value: FIR registered 6 Oct 2013; charges framed; trial concluded in conviction
investigation_status.reason: 'Charge sheet filed' is not stated, though the rest is fine.

appeal_history.correct_value: Sessions Court convicted 30 April 2019; HC (s.482 CrPC) allowed furlough 24 June 2021; SC allowed State's appeal; conviction appeal pending in HC
appeal_history.quote: The appeal against the respondent’s conviction and the application for suspension of sentence are pending for hearing before the High Court
appeal_history.reason: Broadly right but omits the pending conviction appeal and the s.482 petition.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: State argued that furlough is not a right (Rules 3, 4, 17), can be denied on public peace grounds, and that the earlier HC order did not address the objections
prosecution_argument.quote: Rule 17 ... provides that the Rules do not confer a legal right
prosecution_argument.reason: Captures the public peace argument but omits the main points on rules and no right.

defence_argument.correct_value: Furlough is a matter of right (Rule 3(2) every year after seven years); father's illness; no link to attacks; four earlier releases with no incident
defence_argument.quote: The furlough leave is a matter of right
defence_argument.reason: Omits the main arguments, e.g. that furlough is a matter of right.

legal_principle_applied.quote: The grant of furlough must be balanced against the public interest

precedent_relied_upon.quote: State of Maharashtra v. Suresh Pandurang Darvakar (2006) 4 SCC 776
precedent_relied_upon.reason: All three precedents were discussed and relied on.

judicial_mitigating_factors.correct_value: The court noted the respondent was earlier released for a genuine need regarding his mother's health
judicial_mitigating_factors.quote: The respondent was released earlier this year to accommodate a genuine need to attend to his mother’s health
judicial_mitigating_factors.reason: The court noted some mitigating points, so 'None' is slightly off.

judicial_aggravating_factors.correct_value: Threats to witnesses, mass following, bribery attempts, jail conduct not above reproach — grounds for refusing furlough
judicial_aggravating_factors.quote: there is a reasonable apprehension of a disruption of public peace and tranquillity
judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: The court relied on such factors, so 'None' is wrong.

other_sentence_order.correct_value: Compensation of Rs. 5,00,000 under s.357(3) CrPC to the prosecutrix; sentences concurrent
other_sentence_order.quote: The respondent was directed to pay compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/- under Section 357(3)
other_sentence_order.reason: The judgment records a compensation order.
